request.text:
\Cref{thm:p15-w02b-p15-008-null-modification} proves that a function
equal to a version outside an \(\mathcal F_0\)-null set is a version
exactly when it is \(\mathcal G\)-measurable, and witnesses the last
sentence with \(\mathcal G=\{\emptyset,\Omega\}\) on \([0,1]\).
The source's decreasing variant, \(C_{\mathcal G}Y_n\downarrow
C_{\mathcal G}Y\) almost everywhere when \(Y_n\downarrow Y\) almost
everywhere with \(E|Y_1|<\infty\) and \(E|Y|<\infty\)
\cite[p.~210]{DurrettPTEAuthor2019}, is
\cref{thm:p15-w02b-p15-008-decreasing}, which also shows that the
hypothesis \(E|Y_1|<\infty\) cannot be dropped.
request.reason: ED26-P15-CH-conditional-expectation-C004 (assessment disputes): the host asserts that arbitrary F_0-null modifications need not preserve G-measurability without a witness, and omits the decreasing variant stated in the remark after Durrett Theorem 4.1.9 (printed p. 210, PDF p. 218). Both are proved in handbook/parts/p15/conditioning-independence-and-information-w02b-p15-008.tex (section sec:p15-w02b-p15-008-version-limits) with annex proofs annex:p15-w02b-p15-008-null-modification and annex:p15-w02b-p15-008-decreasing. Inserted after the theorem so the theorem's own proof obligation is unchanged.
